identity.industry: UNMAPPED:Digital Financial Services / NBFC-led retail digital lending in India

summary.oneLiner: Kissht (OnEMI Technology Solutions) is a technology-enabled lender offering digital personal and business loans to India's young mass-market segment via its mobile app, on-book through RBI-regulated NBFC subsidiary Si Creva and off-book via lending partners.
summary.business: OnEMI Technology Solutions ('Kissht') is a digital, AI/ML-driven lender to India's aspirational mass-market segment, providing unsecured personal loans and secured loans against property through its app. Loans are held on-book (via wholly-owned RBI middle-layer NBFC Si Creva Capital Services) and off-book (100-0 sourcing, co-lending and direct-assignment arrangements with 47 lenders). AUM was Rs 59,557.53 million with 11.17 million customers and 63.73 million registered users as of December 31, 2025.

one-line thesis: First earnings call as a listed company (listed on NSE & BSE 8-May-2026, oversubscribed). FY26 AUM grew 73% YoY / 19% QoQ to ₹7,066cr with PAT up 75% YoY to ₹281cr, alongside *improving* asset quality (GNPA 2.89%→2.12%) — management is deliberately trading yield/margin for higher-quality borrowers and guides to >40% AUM growth in FY27 with GNPA <2.25% and ROA 4.5-5% / ROE 19-21%.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | FY26 (full year) | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| AUM | ₹7,066cr | +73% YoY, +19% QoQ | On-book ₹3,556cr / off-book ₹3,510cr (~50:50) |
| Total income | ₹2,209cr | +63% YoY | |
| Pre-provisioning operating profit | ₹836cr | +54% YoY | |
| PAT | ₹281cr | +75% YoY | Q4 PAT alone: +52% YoY, +7% QoQ |
| ROA (avg assets) | 5% | — | FY27 guide: 4.5-5% |
| ROE (avg equity) | 24% | — | FY27 guide: 19-21% |
| GNPA | 2.12% (from 2.89%) | -77 bps YoY | FY27 target: <2.25% |
| Net NPA | 0.29% | — | |
| Collection efficiency | 97.01% (FY26 close), 97.15% in Q4 | — | DPD-30 basis |
| Disbursals | Q4 ₹3,954cr vs Q3 ₹3,113cr | — | No FY27 disbursal guidance given (AUM is the guided metric) |
| Portfolio yield | ~30-31% in Q4 | -50-75bps QoQ | Deliberate down-trend as mix shifts to higher-quality/lower-yield borrowers |
| Spread (yield − cost of borrowing) | ~18-19% near term | — | Guided to compress toward ~14-16% NIM spread over 3-4 quarters |
| Net worth | ₹1,343cr | 2.4x over 3 yrs | Organic + retained earnings, plus ₹850cr IPO proceeds |
| Capital adequacy (NBFC) | 25.3% | — | |
> One-offs / distortions called out: (1) OPEX rose in Q4 due to LAP branch build-out (not yet at breakeven) **and** a one-time investment in field-collections headcount aimed at FY27 recovery — management flagged this explicitly as non-recurring in nature. (2) Other income was sequentially lower in Q4, partly explaining the gap between AUM growth (+19% QoQ) and revenue growth (+4-5% QoQ) along with yield compression. (3) The GNPA jump from 0.79% to 2.89% over the last ~2 years was explained as a **write-off policy change** (write-off period extended from 120 to 150 days after auditor discussion) — a technicality, not a credit-quality deterioration, per CFO.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- AUM growth: north of 40% in FY27 (secured + unsecured combined).
- Asset quality: GNPA target <2.25%; YoY reduction in impairment cost of 10-15%; continued improvement in Stage-1 mix.
- Profitability: ROA 4.5-5% (overall book, including lower-ROA secured mix); ROE 19-21%.
- No disbursement guidance provided (deliberate — AUM is the guided KPI, since tenure/ticket-size mix shifts as book matures).
- Rating: cautiously optimistic on a further upgrade from CRISIL/India Ratings within FY27 (active discussion over next 6-8 months); prior CRISIL A- upgrade (Feb-2026) already yielding ~200bps improvement in marginal cost of borrowing; a further upgrade could add 100-150bps reduction, more likely visible in FY28.
- Portfolio yield/spread: origination yield trending down (Q3→Q4 trend cited as "symbolic" of trajectory for next 4-6 quarters); spread (yield − COB) guided toward ~18-19% near term, compressing to ~14-16% longer term as cost of funds and operating leverage improve.
order book & pipeline: Not applicable (lending business — AUM/disbursal figures above serve as the equivalent pipeline metrics).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Unsecured personal loans** — core business; ~45% of loans for business purposes, 30% consumption, 15% emergency, 10% other. ~50% of borrowers salaried, average age 32, average CIBIL 746. 81% of borrowers from top-100 cities. 11.76 million unique customers served to date; 3.5 million active at any time.
- **LAP (Loan Against Property)** — started ~2 years ago; AUM ~₹518cr across 98 branches in 8 states (Karnataka, AP, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, UP, Maharashtra), 7.3% of total AUM. LTV conservative at ~48%, expected to stay range-bound (ticket size ₹6-10 lakh against property valued ₹12-25 lakh). >40% of LAP customers are existing Kissht personal-loan customers (organic, low CAC). Plans to add ~80 more branches in FY27 (from 98); LAP to remain a small % of AUM through FY27. Not yet at steady-state ROA — management expects "a year or two away."
- **Si Creva Capital Services** (100% NBFC subsidiary) — houses on-book lending; ~₹630cr (75% of primary IPO issue) already infused as fresh equity.
- **New wealth/MF-distribution subsidiary** — freshly incorporated wholly-owned entity to distribute mutual funds/wealth products (regulatory requirement for a separate entity); early-stage, non-lending cross-sell.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Future product roadmap (3-5 year horizon, not immediate): gold loan, business loan, education loan, plus fee-based cross-sell (insurance, mutual-fund distribution) leveraging the existing 11.76 million customer base.
- Off-book funding model: FLDG-based co-lending, ~5% First Loss Default Guarantee, ~100% of off-book AUM covered by FLDG — off-balance-sheet growth not leverage-constrained per management (only capital blocked is the FLDG itself).
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **AI/ML underwriting stack**: 7,000+ variables (bureau, banking flows, device intelligence, transactions, alternate data); evolved from decision-tree → gradient-boosting → transformer-based models; AUC improved from 66% (2023) to 74% now — management claims ~2.5x better risk separation vs bureau-only approaches. FOIR (Fixed Obligation Income Ratio) for new FY26 customers down to 30% from 34%.
- **Collections infrastructure**: 7,000+ field agents, 1,000+ tele-callers, >95% in-house collections across 17,000+ pin codes, field intervention from as early as 5 DPD; AI voice agents in early-bucket tele-collections running at >70% of human recovery efficiency.
- **Scale/data moat**: 60 million registered users' behavioral data underpins the models; large repeat-customer base (3.5m of 11.76m active) gives flexibility to select higher-quality repeat borrowers, supporting stable >50% historical growth.
- **Distribution diversification**: <50% of acquisition via digital marketing; remainder via merchant/e-commerce/aggregator partnerships and a growing organic channel (~30%, rising) — reduces CAC dependence vs pure-digital fintech peers. Sachin Tendulkar brand association cited as trust driver in mass-market/mass-affluent segments.
- Management explicitly positioned this vs named listed competitors **Bajaj (Finance)** and **Chola (Cholamandalam)** in personal loan/LAP — competitive edge claimed on (1) demonstrated credit performance via AI/ML and collections discipline, (2) scale advantage from large repeat-customer base enabling further quality selection.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Total income yield/AUM is being deliberately compressed as the company shifts mix toward higher-quality, lower-yield borrowers — framed as conscious strategy, not competitive pressure.
- Impairment cost / average AUM fell from 9.7% (FY25) to 8.2% (FY26); Q4 alone at 7%.
- First-EMI T90 improved from 1.5% to 0.7% in FY26; bounce rate stable at 13.1%.
- Stage-2 book reduced from 3.5% to 2.4%; Stage-3 from 2.9% to 2.1%. Stage-3 ECL coverage 86.2%; Stage-2 ECL coverage up sharply from 59.2% (Mar-25) to 75.6% (Mar-26); total PCR 86%. Management overlay buffer of ₹136cr carried in addition.
- Q4 OPEX increase driven by (1) LAP branch scale-up (pre-breakeven) and (2) a one-time investment in field-collections headcount for FY27 NPA-recovery build-out.
- Cost of borrowing (on-book, 45+ lending partners): 11.5-14.25%; expected to ease meaningfully following the Feb-2026 CRISIL A- upgrade (~200bps improvement in marginal cost of borrowing already visible).
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- LAP branch network: 98 branches → plan to add ~80 more in FY27, calibrated to existing-geography deepening (not new-state entry) and branch-level profitability/risk signals.
- IPO proceeds (₹850cr): 75% (~₹630cr) already deployed into Si Creva Capital as fresh equity (on-book lending capital); balance 25% earmarked for technology/AI infrastructure, brand-building, customer acquisition and general corporate purposes — management says current capital position is comfortably sufficient to fund the 40% FY27 AUM growth guidance (i.e., no near-term capital raise signaled).
capital allocation:
- IPO proceeds deployment split 75% on-book capital (into NBFC subsidiary) / 25% technology & AI infra (per opening remarks); actual Q4 update: ~₹630cr (75% of primary issue) infused into Si Creva; remaining 25% into tech/AI/brand/CAC/general corporate, deployed in calibrated manner.
- Steady-state target leverage: on-book (personal-loan-heavy) debt/equity of 2.5-3x; potential to improve further as secured (LAP) book scales, described as a "two-year journey." Off-book/FLDG side not leverage-constrained.
risks & watch-items:
- Macro backdrop flagged explicitly by CEO: elevated global rates, oil prices, geopolitical disruption, currency volatility weighing on India — prompted a **7% reduction in disbursements** and a **pause on lending across ~450 pin codes** flagged by early-warning systems in FY26 (framed as proactive, not reactive).
- Yield/margin compression is a self-imposed trend — watch whether ROA guidance (4.5-5%) holds as portfolio yield keeps declining faster than cost-of-funds benefit materializes.
- LAP business not yet at steady-state ROA (~1-2 years out) — a continuing drag on consolidated OPEX/ROA until breakeven.
- GNPA optics: historical 0.79%→2.89% rise attributed to write-off policy change (120→150 days) — worth confirming this doesn't recur/shift again.
- Concentration/competitive risk: explicitly named competitors Bajaj (Finance) and Cholamandalam entering/expanding in personal loan and LAP.
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, and notably risk-first in tone for a first post-IPO call — repeated emphasis on "prudence as competitive advantage," proactive de-risking (pin-code pauses, disbursement pullback) rather than pure growth chase. CFO was transparent and specific in disaggregating OPEX drivers and the GNPA write-off technicality rather than deflecting. Management declined to give disbursement or precise yield-settlement guidance, citing strategic reasons (AUM as the "fulcrum" metric) — a reasonable but slightly guidance-light stance to watch as the story matures.
non-obvious takeaways:
- This is genuinely the company's **first earnings call as a listed entity** (listed 8-May-2026) — all disclosure/guidance frameworks are being established this quarter; useful baseline for future QoQ tracking.
- Deliberate strategy to pass margin benefits (from operating leverage + lower cost of funds) through to customers to acquire better credit quality — i.e., margin compression is being used as a customer-acquisition/quality tool, not merely a competitive response.
- ~45% of active customers already carry another (larger-ticket) personal loan from elsewhere — signals significant multi-lender exposure among borrowers, worth monitoring systemically.
- NACH coverage is 100% of customers (~3.5 million monthly NACH presentations) — full automated-debit collection infrastructure already in place.

one_liner.body: Kissht (OnEMI Technology Solutions) is a technology-enabled lender offering digital personal and business loans to India's young mass-market segment via its mobile app, on-book through RBI-regulated NBFC subsidiary Si Creva and off-book via lending partners.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: OnEMI Technology Solutions ('Kissht') is a digital, AI/ML-driven lender to India's aspirational mass-market segment, providing unsecured personal loans and secured loans against property through its app. Loans are held on-book (via wholly-owned RBI middle-layer NBFC Si Creva Capital Services) and off-book (100-0 sourcing, co-lending and direct-assignment arrangements with 47 lenders). AUM was Rs 59,557.53 million with 11.17 million customers and 63.73 million registered users as of December 31, 2025.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body: - Si Creva Capital Services Private Limited — Wholly-owned subsidiary (RBI middle-layer NBFC): Holds on-book loan portfolio

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Unsecured:** Personal loans (94.23% of AUM as of Dec 31, 2025)
- **Secured:** Loan against property / LAP (5.77% of AUM)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Mass-market retail borrowers (avg age 32, median CIBIL 746; 67.65% earning Rs 25k-75k/month; 63.38% in top-50 cities)
- Small business / merchant borrowers

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Vertically integrated tech-lending stack (in-house LOS, LMS and Automated Collections System). Funding integration: on-book via wholly-owned NBFC Si Creva and off-book via 47 lending partners under 100-0 sourcing, co-lending and direct-assignment arrangements. Distribution via omni-channel acquisition (digital, 52,396 active merchants, e-commerce, organic).

customers.title: Oem (RHP)
customers.body:
- Si Creva Capital Services Private Limited (wholly-owned RBI-regulated NBFC subsidiary)
- 47 lending partners (banks, NBFCs, fund houses)
- Vertex Growth Fund (investor)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- AUM growth via customer acquisition and repeat business
- Customer acquisition cost vs lifetime value
- Portfolio/asset quality (Gross NPA 2.90% Dec 2025 vs 0.79% FY24)
- On-book vs off-book mix and cost of funds
- Total income fell 20.44% FY24 to FY25 (mix/disbursement shift)

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Augment Si Creva's capital base to support AUM growth
- Deepen embedded finance via API-first merchant/e-commerce partnerships (52,396 active merchants)
- Expand product suite including secured LAP
- Grow iOS presence (launched Dec 2025)

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Uses net proceeds of the fresh issue (up to Rs 8,500 million) to augment the capital base of subsidiary Si Creva Capital Services to support the growth of its on-book lending business; continues scaling the digital lending platform and lender base rather than physical expansion.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Large customer base (11.17M customers, 63.73M registered users) via diversified multi-channel acquisition (digital, merchant, e-commerce, organic)
- Proprietary AI/ML underwriting (400+ variables, 39 sub-models) with instant decisioning and automated collections (ACS)
- Scalable cloud-native tech platform (99.99% uptime; 331 in-house engineers)
- Balanced on-book/off-book liability profile across 47 lenders
- Strong AUM and PAT growth (AUM CAGR 79.53% FY23-FY25; PAT CAGR 140.95%)
- Marquee backing (Vertex Growth Fund); brand ambassador Sachin Tendulkar; NPS 95, 4.6 Play Store rating

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Unsecured-loan concentration — 94.23% of AUM is unsecured personal loans; higher default risk, no collateral
- Regulatory dependence (RBI) — Digital lending and NBFC subject to evolving RBI regulation; co-lending/DA rules
- Asset quality deterioration — Gross NPA rose to 2.90% (Dec 2025) from 0.79% (FY24)
- Funding access / cost — Dependent on 47 lenders and off-book arrangements; D/E rising to 1.63x
- Customer acquisition cost — Growth depends on cost-effective acquisition and repeat business
- Reliance on commissioned industry report — Industry data from 1Lattice report commissioned by the company

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Augment the capital base of subsidiary Si Creva Capital Services to fund AUM growth from fresh-issue net proceeds.**
- **Expand embedded-finance distribution via merchant and e-commerce partnerships.**
- **Grow secured LAP and iOS app presence alongside core unsecured lending.**
- **Maintain asset quality and provisioning coverage as AUM scales.**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Augment Si Creva's capital base to support AUM growth
- Deepen embedded finance via API-first merchant/e-commerce partnerships (52,396 active merchants)
- Expand product suite including secured LAP
- Grow iOS presence (launched Dec 2025)
